page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-32 is an x86_64 server instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B45 processors. The instance provides 32 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features a cache architecture of 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 252 GB, which supplies roughly 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware vector extensions include AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16 formats), AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in compute-focused single-core and multi-core operations. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved a single-core score of 2591.0 and a multi-core score of 21815.0, placing it in the top 10 percent of recorded systems. Compression operations are similarly robust, reaching 37.92 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 218.62 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Static web serving throughput reached 43.98 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng results and database transaction benchmarks landed within the middle 50 percent, while large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 101.71 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU ratio allows resource-intensive applications to run without requiring the over-provisioning of excess CPU cores to access sufficient memory. However, the architectural absence of attached NVMe storage requires external persistent storage disks, introducing network storage latency into the I/O path. Memory bandwidth scales moderately for large uncached transfers compared to memory-bound high-bandwidth architectures.

The c4d-highmem-32 instance fits large memory footprints requiring consistent dedicated compute. Primary application fits include in-memory databases, large caching layers such as Redis, CI/CD compilation workloads, large-scale data transformation, and small-model CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-32 is an x86_64 instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B45 processors, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 252 GB of system memory. It incorporates modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, VNNI, and SHA-NI, but does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the platform achieves top-tier results in single-core and multi-core Geekbench suites, alongside strong software compilation metrics and single-threaded compression throughput. Conversely, multi-core stress testing and large-block uncached memory bandwidth perform within average industry bands. Offering 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance yields high memory density relative to compute allocation, avoiding the need to over-provision CPU cores purely for memory capacity. This profile aligns with memory-heavy enterprise tasks, including in-memory databases, large Redis deployments, distributed build workflows, and CPU-driven small model machine learning inference.
